author: SHINNI9AMI
quote:
30fps in 2026 is indefensible. Every console version is locked to it, with no performance mode, so a flagship that looks gorgeous in screenshots feels dated the moment you move the camera. After a 13-year wait, smoothness shouldn’t be a premium feature.
The story is the other letdown. Jason and Lucia’s relationship plays like a simp simulator. For me it felt like a romance first and a crime game second, and the chaos and heists that made GTA what it is took a back seat to long drives and chores. 

GTA built its name on freedom, and GTA 6 trades a lot of it for realism. Street prostitution, in every 3D GTA since 2001, is gone, and Rockstar says it only kept features that suit Jason and Lucia’s story. Rampages and carrying unlimited weapons are gone too, and pedestrians now react the moment you pull out a gun, so the old do-whatever-you-want chaos feels policed rather than playful. Killing anyone is still possible, but your actions are tracked and carry lasting consequences, which feels like the opposite of the sandbox that made this series. The strip clubs survive; the mischief doesn’t.

Beautiful graphics, but hollow where it counts. Not worth full price.
